global_layoffs.description: Barclays announced that approximately 5,000 roles would be replaced by AI as part of workforce and operating-model changes.
Virgin Media O2 confirmed plans to cut thousands of jobs while pursuing substantial cost savings and technology-driven efficiency.
Qantas announced 850 job cuts under an Accenture agreement that moves work offshore and incorporates technology-enabled process changes.
Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to approximately 60,000 eligible employees while controlling costs and funding increased artificial-intelligence investment.
Salesforce reduced its customer-support workforce from about 9,000 to about 5,000 as its chief executive cited reduced headcount needs from AI.
SUSE was identified in a November layoff compilation as an employer explicitly attributing a workforce reduction to AI, but the available report did not provide a reliable job count.
Recent workforce reductions at Bunnings were linked in reporting to AI disruption and technological change, without a verified job count in the available source.
Canva was among Australian companies whose recent job cuts were associated in reporting with AI disruption and technological change, without a verified job count.

saudi_policy_updates.title: Higher Saudi worker counting thresholds under Nitaqat
saudi_policy_updates.description: The minimum monthly salary for a Saudi employee to count as one full worker is scheduled to rise from SAR 4,000 to SAR 5,000 and later SAR 6,000.

ai_workforce_signals.headline: Integrated AI adoption linked to planned headcount reductions
ai_workforce_signals.description: A CIPD survey of more than 2,000 British employers found that 32% of firms with integrated AI planned workforce reductions, compared with 5% among firms that did not use AI. Nearly half of strategically adopting firms expected to cut staff.

ai_workforce_signals.headline: AI increasingly associated with lower headcount
ai_workforce_signals.description: BSI research found that 54% of business leaders said AI was helping reduce headcount, up from 41% the previous year. The research also indicated that entry-level opportunities were being reduced.

ai_workforce_signals.headline: AI displacement is appearing through weaker hiring
ai_workforce_signals.description: Research summarized in an AI-and-work review found unemployment rising more among workers in occupations highly exposed to generative AI, with younger workers showing a larger differential. The evidence indicates reduced job-finding rates may precede large-scale layoffs.

ai_workforce_signals.headline: Anthropic reports extensive AI-written code
ai_workforce_signals.description: A policy report cited Anthropic as claiming that more than 90% of changes merged into its core codebase were written by Claude with human guidance. The development signals accelerating automation of software-production tasks.

ai_workforce_signals.headline: China considers transition protections for AI deployment
ai_workforce_signals.description: China’s State Council was reported to have called on firms to explore an unemployment-buffer period when deploying AI at scale. Proposed measures include advance notice and retraining programs.

ai_workforce_signals.headline: AI adoption is reducing entry-level opportunity
ai_workforce_signals.description: BSI-related reporting said nearly half of surveyed business leaders believed AI had already reduced entry-level opportunities. This raises workforce-pipeline risks for employers implementing AI-led productivity programs.

ai_workforce_signals.headline: US payroll growth affected by AI exposure
ai_workforce_signals.description: A reported estimate attributed approximately 16,000 fewer monthly US payroll additions over the prior year to artificial intelligence and linked the effect to a 0.1-percentage-point increase in unemployment. The estimate indicates labor-market effects may be visible in hiring before formal layoffs.

weekly_stats.notable_trend: AI-related workforce pressure is broadening from explicit technology-sector cuts into customer support, software production, and entry-level hiring, while Gulf-specific automation and Saudi policy activity remained limited in the available reporting.
